title: Certified cells, a tiered display and a settled telephoto
summary: Chinese certification puts the Pro alongside the Ultra at 60 W with larger rated cells. The display story splits into tiers the way the leaks once said it would not. Two named tipsters push the 4x telephoto report aside, and the base model's own spec sheet starts to look cheaper, not newer.

claims.title: An Exynos Ultra may be back on the table
claims.summary: Money Today reports development of an Exynos 2700 Galaxy S27 Ultra for some markets, alongside the Snapdragon model. Android Authority highlights the change against earlier Snapdragon-only expectations.
claims.assessment: Specific industry reporting, but a development order is not a retail launch. Regions, chip branding and sustained performance remain unconfirmed.

claims.title: A wider camera island, not isolated rings
claims.summary: SamMobile describes OnLeaks-based CAD renders with a horizontal rectangular rear camera bar. Android Authority separately describes Sonny Dickson images with a wide camera plateau.
claims.assessment: Two attributed image-report chains point in a similar direction, but neither establishes the final production design. We could not inspect the original Android Headlines article.

claims.title: Three rear cameras in the newer render report
claims.summary: SamMobile describes three rear cameras in the reported CAD-based design. That conflicts with Android Central’s earlier description of a main camera plus three 50-megapixel lenses.
claims.assessment: Counting lenses in an alleged design is not a confirmed camera specification. Both accounts are retained; the newer article alone does not settle it, and the September telephoto reporting disputes the module behind the third lens while leaving the count itself open.

claims.title: Built-in magnetic charging is suggested
claims.summary: Android Authority interprets a circular rear cutout in the apparent renders as possible integrated Qi2 magnets. SamMobile says 25-watt Qi2 charging is likely.
claims.assessment: This is an interpretation of images and secondary reporting, not certification or a verified charging test. No charging speed is treated as established.

claims.title: The earlier account still described four lenses
claims.summary: Android Central’s report of Anthony’s tip lists a 200-megapixel main camera and three 50-megapixel lenses: ultrawide, 5× telephoto and another telephoto.
claims.assessment: Retained as a conflicting report, not silently deleted or declared false. The later three-camera account has not been officially resolved.

claims.title: Snapdragon-only expectations are now challenged
claims.summary: Android Central’s earlier specification report names Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro for Galaxy without an Exynos variant. Android Authority explicitly says the newer Exynos report contradicts prior Snapdragon-only claims.
claims.assessment: The earlier specification list is not proof of worldwide exclusivity. Snapdragon and Exynos may coexist; naming and regional availability remain unsettled.

claims.title: A 6.9-inch Privacy Display is tipped
claims.summary: Android Central reports Anthony’s claim of a 6.9-inch QHD+ Privacy Display for the Ultra.
claims.assessment: One tipster chain, no panel document or production unit examined. The September ETNews reading now narrows Privacy Display to the Pro and Ultra, so the all-models account is preserved here as the contradicted side of a live disagreement rather than as a settled display specification.

claims.title: 5,534 mAh rated; advertised capacity still an estimate
claims.summary: GalaxyClub says information it viewed gives the Ultra a 5,534 mAh rated battery. It estimates an advertised capacity around 5,700 mAh, possibly 5,800 mAh; Android Authority relays the 5,700 mAh estimate.
claims.assessment: Rated and typical capacity are different measures. The original article's second "rated" label is internally inconsistent; we preserve its estimates while noting that the 5,534 mAh rated figure now also appears in the September 3C coverage, which is firmer provenance than the July relay.

claims.title: Silicon-carbon chemistry is plausible, not demonstrated
claims.summary: GalaxyClub infers silicon-carbon chemistry indirectly from the reported capacity increase. 9to5Google also relays a silicon-carbon rumor, noting that lineup coverage and capacities were unclear.
claims.assessment: A capacity estimate does not prove cell chemistry. This is a separate, lower-confidence claim from the rated-capacity report.

claims.title: A 16-megapixel front camera is reported
claims.summary: 9to5Google’s roundup lists a 16-megapixel autofocus selfie camera for the Ultra. GalaxyClub also describes a new 16-megapixel front camera.
claims.assessment: These reports share GalaxyClub provenance. Sensor shape and stabilization are not established by this record.

claims.title: A new Pro turns the family's trio into a quartet
claims.summary: CAD render reports describe four Galaxy S27 models instead of three: the base S27, an S27+, a new S27 Pro and the S27 Ultra. GSMArena describes the Pro as a smaller Ultra without an S Pen, and Android Headlines reads the Plus CAD as proof the Plus survives. SamMobile's case images show the same quartet.
claims.assessment: Several outlets agree on a four-model reading, but they are reading render art rather than a Samsung document, and the segmentation is inferred from images. A rumored S27 Edge would make five. Nothing here is an announcement.

claims.title: The base S27 barely leaves the S26 behind
claims.summary: CAD renders of the base S27 show an oval three-ring camera bump in the top-left corner, flat panels and a flat frame, with reported dimensions of 149.75 × 71.88 × 7.25 mm and a 6.3-inch display. 9to5Google notes the base model looks nothing like the redesigned Ultra.
claims.assessment: Three outlets describe the same Android Headlines render set, so this is shared provenance rather than three independent leaks. The dimensions are render-derived and the chipset is still described as open.

claims.title: The Pro inherits the Ultra's body but not its periscope
claims.summary: GSMArena reports the S27 Pro at 154.06 × 73.77 × 7.95 mm with a roughly 6.6-inch display, sharing the Ultra's 200-megapixel main and 50-megapixel ultrawide but using a 12-megapixel 3x telephoto instead of a periscope, plus a rumored 5,200 mAh battery. SamMobile's case-render report says 5x optical zoom may stay exclusive to the Ultra.
claims.assessment: Two outlets point the same way and neither examined hardware. The discriminating claim is the telephoto, which is why this is filed under cameras; the size and battery figures remain renderer claims and the Ultra's own zoom arrangement is unresolved.

claims.title: A camera plateau may replace the horizontal bar
claims.summary: Notebookcheck reports that an Ice Universe design sketch, which the leaker later said was the S27 Ultra, shows a raised camera plateau closer to Apple's iPhone 17 Pro treatment, and that the earlier Pixel-like horizontal bar is out. SamMobile's 2 September case images show the Pro and Ultra with the same raised plateau.
claims.assessment: This directly conflicts with the OnLeaks CAD camera bar already in this archive. Two of the best-known render sources currently point at different rear designs, so the conflict is preserved rather than resolved. None of it is official evidence.

claims.title: An S27 Edge is rumored, and the two accounts disagree
claims.summary: Two X accounts posted on 2 September that a Galaxy S27 Edge is in development for 2027. @kro_roe described a 5.8-inch display in a low-4 mm chassis with a 4,300 mAh battery; @SPYGO19726 replied hours later claiming a 6.8-inch body at 5.4 mm. SamMobile, Notebookcheck and tech-ish all report both readings.
claims.assessment: Neither account gave a source, and the two readings differ on the most basic property of the device. The archive keeps both opposed instead of choosing one. Notebookcheck calls this the only very early rumor in the family. An Edge would likely arrive later in 2027 than the main quartet.

claims.title: Charging stays at 25 W and 45 W
claims.summary: Android Authority reports that China's 3C registry lists 25 W wired charging for the base S27 and 45 W for the S27 Plus, relayed from tipster Abhishek Yadav on X. The report notes the base model would still trail the Galaxy S26 FE, and that the S27 Ultra and Pro may keep or improve on last year's 60 W.
claims.assessment: A regulatory listing is firmer evidence than a render, but this archive did not inspect the registry entry and the relay is a single chain. The same registry later put the Pro and Ultra at 60 W, which the base model's 25 W does not share.

claims.title: Magnetic arrays are read into all four CAD sets
claims.summary: Notebookcheck's reading of the Ice Universe CAD renders says all four S27 models include built-in magnetic arrays for magnetic chargers and accessories. Android Authority separately reports built-in magnets for MagSafe-style latching across the series, though it says wireless charging speed may not change.
claims.assessment: This extends the earlier Qi2 interpretation from a circular cutout on the Ultra to the whole family. CAD geometry is not certification, and the archive still holds no charging test or certification document.

claims.title: The speaker grille moves to the right on three models
claims.summary: Notebookcheck reports that in the leaked CAD renders the base S27, the S27+ and the rumored S27 Pro move the bottom-firing speaker grille to the right of the USB-C port, while the Ultra keeps the left-side placement used on the S26 generation.
claims.assessment: One outlet's reading of CAD geometry, with an ergonomic rationale attached to it. Useful as a design detail, but it is not a measured audio specification and the archive has not seen a teardown or part listing.

claims.title: A leaked die shot fixes the Exynos 2700's outline
claims.summary: SamMobile reports that a SemiAnalysis die shot and annotated floorplan show the Exynos 2700 with a 10-core CPU (two C2 Ultra cores at 4.24 GHz and 3.36 GHz, eight C2 Pro cores), an Xclipse 970 GPU with 16 compute units, a 24 MB system-level cache, four LPDDR6 PHYs and no integrated modem, built on Samsung Foundry's SF2P 2 nm process.
claims.assessment: An inspectable floorplan is firmer evidence than a text tip, but it is still a leak, and claims that the chip beats Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 are not measured. The archive attaches this to the chipset question rather than to a shipping part.

claims.title: The base S27 is tipped for a 4,900 mAh cell and a Sony sensor
claims.summary: GSMArena relays that the base S27 may use a new Sony main camera sensor and a silicon-carbon battery at 4,900 mAh, up from the S26's 4,300 mAh, while leaving the chipset open between Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Exynos 2700. tech-ish separately relays a July report saying Samsung was undecided about silicon-carbon on the base model because of cost.
claims.assessment: One relayed claim set attached to a render report. A September reading of the 3C filings puts the base model at 4,300 mAh instead, so the 4,900 mAh figure is retained only as the contradicted side of the disagreement, and the chemistry decision is described elsewhere as unresolved on cost.

claims.title: M16 OLED for the Pro and Ultra, M14 for the base and Plus
claims.summary: ETNews reports that Samsung Display will supply M16 OLED panels for the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, with Color Filter-on-Encapsulation and Privacy Display, while the base S27 and S27 Plus move up from M13 to M14. Notebookcheck and SamMobile repeat the split the same day.
claims.assessment: One Korean industry-sourcing chain relayed by several outlets within hours, so the repetition is not independent corroboration. The tier split is specific and internally consistent, and M16 already ships in rival handsets, but no panel specification is officially confirmed.

claims.title: Privacy Display narrows to the Pro and Ultra
claims.summary: Reporting traced to ETNews and read through GSMArena, SamMobile and Notebookcheck says only the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra get Privacy Display, leaving the base and Plus out. That reverses a July report that every model except a future FE would carry it, and a mid-September round-up still repeats the all-models version.
claims.assessment: The newer claim is the more specific one - Flex Magic Pixel panels plus COE on two models - but it comes from the same sourcing chain that has now changed twice. The archive keeps both readings open and does not treat the July account as dead.

claims.title: The four models' screen sizes take shape
claims.summary: ETNews lists a 6.27-inch Galaxy S27, a 6.66-inch S27 Plus, a 6.47-inch S27 Pro and a 6.89-inch S27 Ultra, with Samsung Display expected to supply every panel. SamMobile repeats the same four figures and Notebookcheck reports the same range.
claims.assessment: Panel-supply reporting usually carries firmer dimensions than render-based guesses, and a Pro that lands smaller than the Plus matches the design story, but these are unannounced sizes from a single sourcing chain.

claims.title: 3C listings give the Pro and Ultra 60 W and larger rated cells
claims.summary: China's 3C registry entries linked to SM-S957 and SM-S958 show 60 W wired charging at 20 V/3 A for both the Galaxy S27 Pro and S27 Ultra, and separate battery filings are reported at 5,087 mAh rated for the Pro and 5,534 mAh rated for the Ultra - figures outlets convert to roughly 5,200 mAh and 5,700 mAh advertised.
claims.assessment: A regulatory filing is stronger evidence than a tip, but this archive did not inspect the registry entry and the model-number mapping is an outlet inference. Rated and expected advertised capacities stay separate, and the 60 W ceiling only matches what the S26 Ultra already offers.

claims.title: A single 4x telephoto was under evaluation for the Ultra
claims.summary: A late-August tip attributed to @phonefuturist described Samsung weighing one 50-megapixel 1/1.9-inch telephoto at 4x optical zoom in place of the Ultra's separate 3x and 5x cameras, with five Ultra prototypes in test and a hardware decision said to be due around 9 September.
claims.assessment: An account-level tip read only through relays, with no document behind it. The surrounding write-ups make clear the configuration was being compared against the existing 5x module on cost, not chosen.

claims.title: The 5x telephoto looks set to carry over after all
claims.summary: Ice Universe called the 4x 1/1.9-inch report false and said the Ultra keeps its 5x 1/2.52-inch module; two days later two outlets attributed the same 50-megapixel Sony 5x arrangement to Roland Quandt. GSMArena also records the Pro as a 200-megapixel main, 50-megapixel ultrawide and 12-megapixel 3x telephoto.
claims.assessment: Two named accounts with long track records point the same way, which is the strongest camera signal of the week - yet neither original post was read, the 3x removal Ice Universe previously asserted is untouched here, and a carried-over module changes nothing buyers can check before launch.

claims.title: Warmer colour and reworked Log video are tipped for the Ultra
claims.summary: An X account, @WalleGalaxy, says the S27 Ultra keeps 4K/120fps and 8K/30fps while gaining updated Samsung Log and APV support for wider dynamic range, plus an overhauled photo pipeline tuned for warmer, more natural colour than the S26 Ultra. A 16-megapixel autofocus selfie camera is repeated alongside.
claims.assessment: The camera count and front-camera details overlap with earlier chains, but the colour and codec claims rest on one account that Android Authority itself flags as not established. Software tuning cannot be checked before launch, and no Samsung statement covers it.

claims.title: A 7,000 mAh, S Pen-less prototype was reportedly rejected
claims.summary: Android Police, relaying X user Kro and Android Authority, reports that Samsung tested Galaxy S27 Ultra units without an S Pen slot and with a 7,000 mAh cell, then settled on a 5,700-6,000 mAh target with silicon-carbon anode chemistry of the kind used in the Fold 8 generation.
claims.assessment: The rejected prototype would explain why earlier capacity chatter ranged so widely, but the account published no document and the surviving figure is a target rather than a specification. Chemistry is inferred from another product line, not from a filing.

claims.title: The base S27's display may be engineered down to a price
claims.summary: PhoneArena's running round-up says Samsung is weighing BOE panels for the base model, may leave it on the older M13 material and is evaluating third-party display driver ICs from Anapass, DB Global Chip, Wonik D2I and Novatek - measures that would sit against the M14 upgrade reported for the base and Plus.
claims.assessment: Each item is individually uncorroborated and presented as an option rather than a decision. If any of it lands, the base model's screen would be the first part of the family to move backwards, so the archive holds it against the ETNews M14 claim without settling the question.

claims.title: LPDDR5X for the base and Plus, LPDDR6 held for the Ultra
claims.summary: PhoneArena, citing the Korean outlet The Bell, reports Samsung qualifying Micron LPDDR5X for the Galaxy S27 series and reserving LPDDR6 for the Ultra tier on cost grounds, with Micron's opening pricing described as well above Samsung's own memory division.
claims.assessment: A memory-standard split between four flagships would matter over the life of the devices, but it rests on one relayed Korean report and a supplier earnings remark rather than a Samsung statement or a filing this archive read.

claims.title: The chip tiers look set to widen between the Ultra and the rest
claims.summary: PhoneArena's round-up says Qualcomm is splitting Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 into standard and Pro versions, with the Pro part going to the S27 Ultra and the standard part to the base and Plus, while Samsung's own Exynos 2700 evaluation is described as beating both in CPU, GPU, AI and efficiency tests.
claims.assessment: Aggregated from tipsters and Korean supply-chain reporting rather than read at source here. Pre-release benchmark claims about unreleased silicon are the least stable class of leak, and the regional split that decides what buyers actually get is still unconfirmed.

claims.title: The base and Plus cells may be smaller than the archive first heard
claims.summary: A 20 September aggregation of the 3C coverage repeats a readings-based figure of 4,300 mAh for the base model and 4,900 mAh for the Plus, alongside the already-reported 25 W and 45 W charging ceilings. The 4,300 mAh base figure sits against the archive's August reading of 4,900 mAh for the base model.
claims.assessment: Two relayed readings of different filings disagree about the base model, and neither this archive nor the write-up it read inspected the Chinese registry entry. The Plus figure matching the earlier base figure is exactly the kind of coincidence that argues for caution rather than confirmation.

claims.title: Four models on one stage in the first quarter of 2027, an FE later
claims.summary: Reporters converge on a January or February 2027 Unpacked for the Galaxy S27 family, with ETNews saying simply the first quarter and SamMobile describing a five-model year in which an S27 FE follows around mid-2027. Firmware testing for One UI 9.5 is reported to be behind the S26 cycle's pace.
claims.assessment: Launch timing is the easiest claim to get roughly right and the hardest to pin down exactly. No invitation exists, Samsung has said nothing about the S27 series, and the FE reference is a lineup expectation rather than a commitment.

claims.title: A Pro at Ultra money and an Ultra above $1,400 are this week's expectations
claims.summary: A late-August rumor put the expected US ladder at $899 for the Galaxy S27, $1,099 for the Plus, $1,299 for the Pro and $1,499 for the Ultra, with the new Pro taking the Ultra's old slot. A mid-September round-up, by contrast, says nothing has leaked on base and Plus pricing and that the S26's post-increase levels may simply hold.
claims.assessment: Both readings are expectations, not listings or filings, and they disagree about how much has actually been learned. Component cost pressure is cited on both sides, so the archive records the ladder as a rumor and marks the base and Plus figures as unverified.
